answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% spend reduction, which requires a structural cost move, not a deferral or pure negotiation. Memory c2 documents that a prior primary-vendor switch produced sharp unit-cost reductions with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — i.e., low delivery risk for a move of this kind. With only one decision available this cycle, the cost objective dominates and the switch is the action most directly aligned with the 18% mandate. Verification budget is allocated to c2 because the magnitude of last year's unit-cost cut is the key input to whether this action can plausibly close the 18% gap. Delivery-risk protections: scope the switch as a small guarded test behind the 14-day contract window (or run parallel qualification) so the incumbent remains live as continuity cover until the new vendor is validated, given the 94% utilization has no buffer. If verification of c2 shows last year's cut was materially smaller than 18%, I will downgrade to negotiate_terms with the incumbent before any switch.
